devices.duplicate_id_text: A device with id "{id}" already exists. Enter a unique id.
devices.style_tooltip:
MAINTAINED - energized = ON (one coil), or one coil per direction held energized (two outputs).
PULSE - a pulse per direction, separate coils; ON only when there is one output.
PULSE_TOGGLE - ONE impulse-relay coil (R15/3P-class) behind one or two outputs: every pulse toggles, so the runtime pulses only when the feedback (first feedback point = CLOSED contact) says the device is not already in the requested state. Feedback is mandatory.

zones.sounder_hint: The controller does not drive a siren. It publishes the sounder's state - SSWIN.SIREN_ACTIVE, SIREN_TIME_LEFT, STROBE_ACTIVE, PANIC - and you wire that to an output in Logic Studio, through whatever interlocks the installation needs.

wizard.title: Device Wizard
wizard.intro_text:
It walks you through the configuration in the order the project needs it:

1. Project information - name and author.
2. Device composition - which modules this controller has.
3. I/O cards - the physical modules with their channel kinds and counts. Name the place each one sits in as you go.
4. Locations - describe the places the cards named.

Cards give birth to points: every channel you declare here appears in the Point Registry automatically. Describing those points, wiring apparatus to them, drawing screens and building the logic all happen afterwards, in their own branches of the tree - the last page tells you where.
wizard.info_subtitle: The name is what the controller reports as its project; the author is for the record.
wizard.info_name_required: Enter a project name to continue.
wizard.modules_subtitle: Tick the modules this controller actually has. A module outside the composition does not exist in the project - its branch is not shown at all. Modules already in the project stay ticked; remove one from the Device Composition branch, not here.
wizard.locations_subtitle: Each location is a short code (letters A-Z and digits only, e.g. KOT for the boiler room) plus a description. The codes your cards already named are listed here - give them a description. A card sits in one location; every point on it inherits that location unless you override it later in the Point Registry.
wizard.locations_invalid: Location "{code}": code must consist only of letters A-Z and digits.
wizard.locations_duplicate: Location code "{code}" repeats - each code must be unique.
wizard.cards_subtitle: One row per physical module: an id (the first part of every address, e.g. ELA1 -> ELA1.DI.1), the model, which channel kinds it has and how many of each, its Modbus unit address and the location it sits in. A card with both DI and AI is ONE row with both ticked.
wizard.cards_invalid_id: Card "{id}": id must not be empty and must not contain a dot or a space.
wizard.cards_duplicate_id: Card id "{id}" repeats - each id must be unique.
wizard.cards_no_kind: Card "{id}" has no channel kind ticked - tick at least one, with its channel count.
wizard.cards_duplicate_modbus: Modbus address {unit_id} is used by more than one card.
wizard.summary_subtitle: Nothing is written until you press Finish.
wizard.summary_counts: Project "{name}": {modules} module(s), {locations} location(s), {cards} card(s), {points} point(s) will be created.
wizard.summary_next_heading: After Finish, continue in the tree:
wizard.next_points: Point Registry - describe each channel (what is wired to it, technical note, location override).
wizard.next_devices: Apparatus Registry - add the apparatus and assign its points.
wizard.next_alarm: Intrusion Alarm / Protection - only if those modules are in the composition.
wizard.next_screens: Synoptic Diagram - draw the screens and bind symbols to the points.
wizard.next_logic: Logic - build the control logic on the same addresses.
wizard.next_save: Save the project (top toolbar) - the wizard does not save the file itself.

mqtt.intro: The controller's link to an MQTT broker (Home Assistant). A project setting: it travels with the project to the controller, the panel may change it (Engineer, audited), and differences show in Controller → Controller Settings (live).
mqtt.password_note: The broker password is not part of the project - it is entered once on the controller's panel (Settings → MQTT) and stays there.
mqtt.links_hint: A remote MQTT topic feeds a local Link.<id>.In<n> tag of the given type; a value older than "stale after" is marked stale.
mqtt.object_link_tooltip: An object link from controller {source} - edit it under 'Object Links'.
mqtt.object_link_remove_there: This is an object link - remove it under 'Object Links'.

service_notes.intro: The devices' service logbook, written on the controller's panel (Operator or higher). Entries are never edited or deleted - read-only here. New entries arrive with "Receive from Device" or "Take Controller Values".

live.force_mode_text: Forcing overrides input and output states on the controller. Rules: Engineer token only, every force is audited and shown on the cabinet panel; all forces are released when the mode is turned off, when the link to Studio is lost (no heartbeat) and on a controller restart. The protection path is never forced. Enable force mode?
live.preview_not_ready: The screen editor is still loading - try again in a moment.

object_links.intro: One controller's value available on another as a Link.<Id>.In<n> tag - over MQTT: the source publishes its tags, the target subscribes in MQTT Integration (Studio writes the incoming mappings here and never touches manual ones). The Link.* tag works in the target's logic and screens; it is never a command.
object_links.needs_object: Links need a saved object with at least two controllers (File → Add Controller to Object).
object_links.applied: Written into the projects: {details}. Save the object to keep it.
object_links.invalid_same: Pick a source point and a different controller as the target.
object_links.invalid_link_tag: The tag must look like Link.<Id>.In<name>.
object_links.duplicate_link_tag: Tag {tag} is already used on that controller.

protection_tests.intro: The internal Omicron: the controller forces a state, measures the response time and keeps a report. A process protection - its analog point forced past the threshold, the trip timed against the configured delay, then back in band and the reset timed; an apparatus - a command down the same path as from the panel (interlocks and safety checks apply), the feedback timed, then restored. Engineer token, every test audited, reports stay on the controller. The protection path (ADA01) is not covered by this test.
protection_tests.status_idle: Refresh to fetch the list from the controller.
protection_tests.unavailable: This controller has no protection tests (older EPW-OS).
protection_tests.select_row: Select a protection or an apparatus in the list.
protection_tests.no_reports: There are no reports to save.

intrusion.users_intro: Who may arm and disarm which zones. A person's CODE is never part of the project - it is set on the controller itself, so it never travels to Studio, into git or over the network. A user with no zones ticked may operate every zone.
intrusion.line_night_hint: Unticked, this line stops supervising while its zone is armed in night mode - the usual choice for motion detectors inside. A 24-hour line alarms regardless.
